remedy_options: restore a pixel-identical rendering stack (the original bundled operator-tools Mesa/llvmpipe + Xvfb) and re-run GATE A and GATE B
establish, prospectively and before any P2 outcome, an operator-authorised rendering-equivalence rule that the current stack demonstrably satisfies

redesign P2 so that BOTH conditions are captured on one self-consistent apparatus -- but this would require recollecting the wall runs, which the current P2 authority forbids, and would change P2's matched-control design

root_cause.diagnosis: client-side software rasterisation differs; server-side motion is unaffected, which is why coordinates are bit-exact while pixels are not
root_cause.original_gl_stack_location: bundled operator-tools DRI drivers on the wiped NVMe (LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH pointed into operator-tools/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/dri)
root_cause.provenance_gap: mineocclude-capture-runtime-receipt.json pins Java, Minecraft, Fabric and mod hashes but records NO renderer, Mesa, GL, DRI or Xvfb identity, so the original rendering stack cannot be reconstructed from frozen authority

summary: The operator authorised the minimal startspec scene-gating repair, but the rebuilt capture runtime does not reproduce historical rendered pixels. GATE B fails on 14 of 18 hash-bound historical frames, changes the magenta detector area on 11, and flips the detector verdict on 2 occluded frames -- one of which is a frozen Regime A target row (t01, tau=1, frame 43). The same pixels feed MineWorld, so P2 activations captured on this runtime would not be comparable to the historical apparatus.
why_patch_not_applied: the failure is caused by client-side software rasterisation, not by the server mod. Rebuilding the mod cannot change rendered pixels, so applying and building the patch would not have unblocked P2. GATE B was run first because it is cheap and patch-independent, avoiding a Gradle build, 25 captures and all GPU extraction that could not have produced usable data.
